text: app.js buildRow vs styles.css (.tick / .habit-toggle rules): The two files disagree about what a habit row is. styles.css styles `.tick` / `.habit-toggle` as a 44x44 round button that fills with the accent via `[aria-pressed="true"]`, but app.js builds `<label class="habit-toggle">` wrapping a plain `<input type="checkbox">` (.habit-box) plus the name span. Result: the checkbox is unstyled (a default ~13px square), so the round tick described in the CSS never appears; the label inherits width:44px, height:44px and border-radius:50%, so the habit name is squashed and spills out of a small circle; and none of the `[aria-pressed]`/`is-done` button rules can ever match, so there is no filled 'done' tick at all. The row tint (`#habit-list > li.is-done`) does work, but that is the only done cue left.

styles.css — .habit-remove: app.js renders a remove button (`.habit-remove`, an X icon with an aria-label), but styles.css contains no rule for `.habit-remove` or `.habit-remove:hover`/`:focus-visible`. It falls back to the raw browser button: big, grey, mismatched with the card row, with no visible focus ring, which makes the one destructive control in the app both ugly and hard to see.

app.js — list click handler / removeHabit: Clicking the X deletes the habit and its entire day history immediately, with no confirmation and no undo. A misplaced click on a small icon next to every row permanently destroys weeks of streak data, and the `storage` event means other open tabs lose it too. Nothing in index.html or app.js offers a 'sure?' step or an undo.

app.js — setDone / currentStreak (today only): You can only tick or untick today: setDone always uses `today()`, and index.html/app.js offer no day picker or last-seven-days strip. So if you forget to tick yesterday, the day is lost and the streak breaks with no way to repair it — which is exactly the case the streak logic exists to get right. The CSS even reserves room for a `.habit-days` row of day buttons that app.js never renders.

app.js — no date re-check while the page is open: Nothing re-renders at midnight. If the tab is left open overnight, each row still shows yesterday's ticked state, and the first click after midnight calls setDone with the *new* today: unchecking deletes a key that does not exist (silent no-op) while the checkbox and row tint change to unchecked, so the user sees the tick disappear but yesterday's tick is still stored and the summary streak stays. There is no timer or visibility/focus hook to refresh `today()`.

card.title: Second look
agentOnly: The core logic is mostly sound — tick, untick, removal and streak counting across a missed day all work, and all four ids app.js uses (add-habit, habit-name, habit-list, streak-summary) do exist in index.html. The real problems are that app.js renders markup styles.css was never written for (so the round tick and the done state never appear, and the habit name gets crushed into a 44px circle), that removal is instant and irreversible, and that nothing re-checks the date while the page stays open.

Minor: app.js renderList/renderSummary vs styles.css :empty::before: Both empty states are doubled and half of them are dead. app.js already prints 'No habits yet. Add one above to start your first streak.' into #habit-list and 'Add a habit and tick it off to start a streak.' into #streak-summary, so the `:empty::before` placeholders in styles.css never render (the elements are no longer empty). A fresh browser therefore shows two near-duplicate messages at once instead of one clear one.

Minor: styles.css — .habit-streak / .habit-days: styles.css is written for per-habit pieces app.js never produces: a `.habit-streak` badge inside each row ('4 days') and a `.habit-days` grid of day toggles, plus the `#habit-list > li > span:first-child` selector, which no longer matches because the name span is nested inside the label, not a direct child of the li. This dead CSS is also what misleads a reader into thinking a per-row streak is displayed when only the summary panel shows it.

Minor: app.js — loadHabits / saveHabits / start-up guard: Storage problems fail silently. saveHabits only console.errors, so in private mode or when the quota is full the UI shows habits as saved while nothing is written. loadHabits returns [] for a corrupted JSON value or a non-array, quietly discarding every stored habit on one bad byte. And the early `if (!form || !nameInput || !list || !summary) return;` turns any future id rename into a page that looks fine but does nothing, with no message to the user.
